transcript.text: Alright everyone, we're two weeks out from the first production customer launch of the event-ingestion service. We need to finalize the architecture decision today. Per our normal routine, I'd like to hear the final check from application architecture first, and then from compliance. Once I've heard both checks — including any concrete configuration or control actions required for launch — I'll record the operating plan with all of those constraints incorporated. Who's ready to go first?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While testing an unrelated replay tool yesterday, I measured a launch-period burst of about 18,000 events per minute that the hourly batch design cannot process within the customer-facing latency target. The streaming design needs exactly 12 partitions for that load, and the launch plan must include provisioning those 12 partitions and validating replay capacity before launch. I have not yet updated the architecture document because the replay test was outside the launch checklist.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I confirmed with the privacy office this morning that the first customer's event payloads must remain in the EU and be retained for exactly 400 days for an audit requirement. The launch plan must include a data-residency control confirming that payloads remain in the EU. I had not added this to the launch review because the customer questionnaire was completed in a separate compliance system.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Provision exactly 12 partitions for the streaming architecture to handle the launch-period burst of approximately 18,000 events per minute.
Implement and confirm a data-residency control ensuring all event payloads remain in the EU.
Configure event payload retention to exactly 400 days to satisfy the audit requirement.
